doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: What to call the music he plays
summary: They discuss labels like mainstream and classic for tunes largely from the 1920s-40s.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Is this market for — I don’t know what to call it — mainstream I guess — I mean what you’re going to playing tonight, is that a decent word for it?
Yeah, it’s as good as any. I’m not —
Yeah, there’s a lot of different names for it. I don’t really mind any of the titles for it.
It’s basically — correct me if I’m wrong — based on tunes from the ‘30s and ‘40s?
Yeah, even a lot from the ‘20s too. A lot of people think of some songs as being from the ‘40s when they were really written in the ‘20s or even the teens sometimes.
